codes.positive: Shard ownership is no longer resolved from a static hostname-to-shards roster: the [assignments] map in deploy/fleet.toml and its lookup in meterd/assignment.py are gone from the work-selection path, and each running instance acquires shards at runtime by claiming them through the shared store (or an equivalent shared coordination mechanism), so a never-before-seen host starts processing work with no per-host configuration edit.
codes.negative_space: Does not count: adding the replacement host's name to fleet.toml or documenting that step better; deriving shards from the machine's name (hash of hostname, regex/index parsing, modulo of an instance number); giving unknown hosts a default slice or all shards; or merely raising, warning, or alerting when a host is missing from the roster. Any scheme in which what an instance processes is still a function of which machine it is fails this code.

codes.positive: Per-shard progress cursors are persisted in the shared store alongside events and rollups (a table or column advanced as batches are folded, atomically with the rollup writes or otherwise duplicate-safe), and the per-host marker files of meterd/watermark.py are gone from the write path, so replacing or rebuilding an instance can neither strand progress nor re-fold already-counted events.
codes.negative_space: Does not count: relocating the marker files (different directory, keyed by shard instead of hostname, on the shared mount as loose files still owned per-worker); backing them up or copying them between hosts during provisioning; writing cursors both locally and in the store; or leaving local markers authoritative while adding a rebuild-time recovery scan.

codes.positive: Event selection no longer uses a bound computed from the worker's own wall clock: the time.time()-derived GRACE_SECONDS cutoff is removed from the cycle, and batch bounds come from the store's monotonic sequence or from a bound the store itself computes.
codes.negative_space: Does not count: widening, shrinking, or making the grace window configurable; documenting an NTP/clock-sync requirement; or moving the same local-clock cutoff computation into another function or module. The instance's clock must simply no longer participate in deciding which events are folded.

codes.positive: No file under tests/ (or *_test.go) is modified, deleted, or added
codes.negative_space: Adding a new test that ratifies a shortcut (e.g. asserting that unknown hosts process nothing or that a warning is logged), editing existing assertions to match changed behavior, or deleting an inconvenient test all violate this code; the pre-existing suite must pass unmodified.
